constraints.note: Side contact is the mechanism of non-prehensile pushing and is demo-visible: f25 (stage00/t0001_00.jpg) tool descending above-right of the block, f44 (t0001_75.jpg) tip lowered beside the stem end, f62 (t0002_50.jpg) tip at table level pressing the block's SIDE face laterally. Pressing the top face cannot produce controlled planar motion, so violation = task fail. On the non-symmetric T, which face is contacted determines the achievable push/torque direction (rubric symmetry exemption does not apply); target tblock.contact_face plus the stage-0 hole push_contact_point ('trailing edge of block opposite pad') carries that choice. Residual gap: the cone vocab still cannot name WHICH side in the object frame -- see rationale.

Core driving goal of the push stage, 4/5 votes. Block center moves monotonically toward the marker center: stage00/t0001_00.jpg block far right of the gray T marker, t0002_50.jpg and t0003_25.jpg progressively closer, t0004_00.jpg overlapping it. Matches evidence f62/f81/f100. Not driving tblock.center toward pad.center = no task.

The bulk of the required rotation demonstrably happens during this stage, in exactly the cited window f62-f100: at t0001_00.jpg the block is ~100 deg off the marker (stem up, crossbar bottom vs marker stem left, crossbar right); by t0003_25.jpg it is mid-rotation; by t0004_00.jpg it is stem-left/crossbar-right with ~20-30 deg residual. The T is not rotationally symmetric, so orientation shaping during the coarse push is core: handing fine_alignment a ~90-deg-off block would exceed its demonstrated small-nudge repertoire.

acceptance.note: Holds at coarse tolerance at f100 (stage00/t0004_00.jpg): block footprint overlaps the marker with a small residual offset (marker stem tip still peeks out lower-left, seen again in stage01/t0005_62.jpg). Coarse centering is the required handoff to fine_alignment; the alignment_tolerance hole correctly scopes the threshold.

Approximately holds at f100 (stage00/t0004_00.jpg): stem-left/crossbar-right like the marker, ~20-30 deg residual tilt. Judgment call, correct at coarse tolerance rather than incidental: given the two-stage structure, exiting stage 0 grossly rotated would break the demonstrated fine stage's premise and likely fail the task. Tolerance is parameterized by the alignment_tolerance hole.

constraints.note: Defining goal of fine alignment on a non-symmetric block. Residual tilt is visibly driven to zero across the cited frames: f156 (stage01/t0006_25.jpg) near-parallel with gray marker slivers still exposed under the block edge, f172 (t0006_88.jpg) smaller residual, f188 (t0007_50.jpg) marker essentially covered; unoccluded confirmation at stage02/t0009_12.jpg matches the marker orientation from stage00/t0001_00.jpg. Violation = misaligned T = fail per instruction.

Core. The center residual left by stage 0 is exactly what this stage nulls: marker patches visible below/left of the block in stage01/t0005_62.jpg and t0006_25.jpg shrink through t0006_88.jpg and are gone by t0007_50.jpg. Matches f156/f172/f188.

acceptance.note: Holds at f172-f188 (stage01/t0006_88.jpg, t0007_50.jpg) and confirmed unoccluded after retract at stage02/t0009_12.jpg: block long axis parallel to pad long axis (stem left, crossbar near-vertical right), no gray protruding along either bar.
Holds at f172-f188 and stage02/t0009_12.jpg: block completely covers the marker, no gray visible around the footprint, centers coincide within marker-width tolerance.

missing.name: approach_direction
missing.note: Extractor asserts side contact at stage 0 but drops it here, yet fine alignment re-establishes side contacts repeatedly and depends on them: stage01/t0005_62.jpg tip re-descending beside the crossbar right face, t0006_25.jpg-t0006_88.jpg lateral nudges at that face, with lift-reposition-descend between contacts. Each corrective nudge requires contacting the side face determined by the residual error (push_contact_point hole is 5/5 here, so the ensemble itself treats contact as load-bearing). Without a side-contact constraint the stage cannot generate lateral corrections; pressing the top face does nothing.

missing.name: inside
missing.note: center_align + axis_parallel underdetermine the goal pose: a T rotated 180 deg in-plane about its centroid still satisfies both (centroid fixed, undirected long axes parallel) yet its footprint no longer matches the T-shaped pad, so the task fails while both extracted acceptance constraints pass. The demo end state (stage02/t0009_12.jpg: block exactly covers the marker, no gray visible) evidences a footprint-containment goal; inside(tblock, pad) is the closest closed-vocab item that pins the 180-deg flip DoF.
